desc:
Find the length of the shortest contiguous subarray of nums whose largest element minus smallest element is at least d. Return -1 if no subarray qualifies.

nums = [4, 7, 5, 6, 9, 5], d = 5
[4,7,5,6,9] has largest 9, smallest 4, difference 5 -> length 5
no shorter subarray reaches a difference of 5
result = 5
hints: A subarray of length 1 has difference 0, so for d = 0 the answer is 1. For larger d you need at least two elements.
If a subarray reaches spread d, every larger subarray containing it does too. For each right end, you want the largest left end that still satisfies the condition.
Sliding window with a decreasing and an increasing deque: for each right end, while max - min ≥ d, record the length and move the left end forward.
editorial: The property "spread at least d" is monotone in the opposite direction from the usual window problems: growing a subarray can only keep or increase its spread. So for each right end r we want to shrink from the left as long as the window still qualifies. Each time it does, record r - l + 1 and then move l forward by one.

The max and min of the window come from two monotonic deques of indices (decreasing and increasing). When l advances, remove deque fronts whose index is below l. The left pointer never moves backwards: if the window [l, r] was minimal for r, then for r + 1 no start left of l can give a shorter qualifying window. O(n) time, O(n) space.
